To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed speech enhanced deep neural network (SE-DNN) system consistently outperforms state-of-the-art speech recognition approaches in the Aurora4 task.

speech enhanced DNN-HMM systems outperform state-of-the-art systems on all Aurora4 evaluation conditions, and the proposed framework is the first to show such a performance gain without any adaptation or post-processing techniques.
the DNN-based enhancement pre-processing is effective for robust speech recognition, and the performance gain could be further improved by incorporating post-processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two aspects: 1.
the development and investigation of a robust speech recognition system using a speech enhancement front-end.

the following three aspects of the speech recognition system: 1) a speech enhancement pre-processing scheme based on a DNN front-end; 2) a comprehensive study on the speech enhancement pre-processing for different acoustic features and acoustic models; and 3) a study on the robustness of the proposed speech enhancement scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed framework is able to significantly enhance the speech signals and improve the performance of robust speech recognition systems.
DNN-based speech enhancement is a powerful pre-processing technique to improve robustness of speech recognition systems.
the proposed speech enhanced DNN-HMM (SEDNN) framework is a robust and effective speech recognition system for noisy environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the effectiveness of DNNs for speech enhancement and its application to robust speech recognition.
DNNs are very effective in learning the mapping from noisy speech to clean speech and the enhanced speech features can be used directly in HMM training to achieve robustness against noise.
the proposed speech enhancement front-end can be used in a wide range of speech applications to improve the robustness of speech recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed enhancement pre-processor is a simple yet effective approach that can be easily integrated into the current DNN-HMM framework for robust speech recognition.
the proposed enhancement pre-processor can be used as a plug-and-play front-end for speech recognition systems to enhance their performance in noisy environments.
the proposed enhancement scheme is a general pre-processing technique that could be used to improve the performance of speech recognition systems in various conditions.
